findings.highlight: I go through the gate
findings.evidenceJa: 余裕を持って正門を通り抜け
findings.governingReading: Shirou passes through the front gate with time to spare.
findings.explanation: The English omits 余裕を持って, removing the calm timing that contrasts with his sudden unease.

findings.highlight: It feels like the students, and even the trees and the buildings, are dull in color.
findings.evidenceJa: どこか色あせて見えるような錯覚だった。
findings.governingReading: Shirou experiences an illusion as though the students, trees, and school building look faded.
findings.explanation: The English drops 錯覚 and presents the fading as a direct felt property, weakening the explicit uncertainty of the supernatural symptom.

findings.highlight: I’m sure that I’m stressed out from all the events that have been happening.
findings.evidenceJa: 色々あって過敏になってるのかもしれない
findings.governingReading: Shirou considers that recent events may have made him oversensitive.
findings.explanation: The English changes tentative oversensitivity into certainty that he is stressed, altering both modality and diagnosis.

findings.highlight: I close my eyes and rotate my shoulders.
findings.evidenceJa: ポキポキと肩を鳴らす。
findings.governingReading: Shirou cracks his shoulders with audible pops.
findings.explanation: The English replaces the concrete sound and action with rotating his shoulders.

findings.highlight: even after that
findings.evidenceJa: そうやって一呼吸おいて見ても
findings.governingReading: Even after pausing for a breath and looking again.
findings.explanation: “After that” removes both the deliberate pause and the second act of looking used to test the sensation.

findings.highlight: I know her, so I greet her.
findings.evidenceJa: 一応、もう顔見知りなワケだし軽く挨拶をする。
findings.governingReading: Since they are at least acquainted now, Shirou gives Rin a light greeting.
findings.explanation: The English removes 一応 and 軽く, flattening the tentative social calibration behind his casual greeting.

findings.highlight: She looks away from me and goes back to her classroom.
findings.evidenceJa: ふん、と顔を背けて自分の教室へと戻っていった。
findings.governingReading: Rin turns away with a dismissive snort and returns to her classroom.
findings.explanation: The English omits the audible ふん that marks her deliberate irritation and embarrassment.

findings.highlight: Shinji is actually quite punctual and he tries hard to follow the rules.
findings.evidenceJa: 慎二は几帳面で、神経質なまでに規則を守ろうとするヤツだ。
findings.governingReading: Shinji is methodical and tries to follow rules to an almost neurotic degree.
findings.explanation: “Punctual” narrows 几帳面, while “tries hard” omits the excessive, anxious force of 神経質なまでに, softening a character judgment that makes his absence suspicious.

findings.highlight: Issei then puts his head on the table.
findings.evidenceJa: べったりと机に伏したまま、一成はそんな事を言う。
findings.governingReading: Still sprawled flat against the desk, Issei says this.
findings.explanation: The English makes the posture a subsequent action and reduces his whole-body, stuck-flat state to placing his head down.

findings.highlight: I thought you had to go to bed at eleven at the temple.
findings.evidenceJa: お山じゃ十一時には絶対就寝じゃなかったっけ？
findings.governingReading: Shirou recalls that up on the mountain bedtime is absolutely at eleven.
findings.explanation: The English replaces Shirou’s familiar お山 register with “the temple” and drops 絶対, weakening the teasing reference to Issei’s strict routine.

findings.highlight: I’m having difficulty sleeping lately.
findings.evidenceJa: 最近寝付きが良くない。
findings.governingReading: Recently Issei has trouble falling asleep.
findings.explanation: The English broadens sleep-onset difficulty into general difficulty sleeping, blurring the symptom.

findings.highlight: You certainly got me there.
findings.evidenceJa: まことに耳が痛い
findings.governingReading: The spring-sleep quotation hits painfully close to home for Issei.
findings.explanation: “Got me there” recasts his rueful recognition as losing a verbal point, flattening the formal allusive voice.

findings.highlight: I’ll stay here until lunch is over
findings.evidenceJa: 昼休みが終わるまで付き合うとするか
findings.governingReading: Shirou decides to keep Issei company until lunch ends.
findings.explanation: Generic staying removes 付き合う and the small act of companionship.

findings.highlight: Tell them the student council isn’t open today.
findings.evidenceJa: 生徒会は店じまいだと言ってやれ
findings.governingReading: Issei tells Shirou to say the student council has closed up shop.
findings.explanation: The English conveys closure but removes the comic commercial metaphor 店じまい.

findings.highlight: . Hm, that’s bad.
findings.evidenceJa: 。むむ、それはまずい
findings.governingReading: Issei reacts, “Mm, that is bad.”
findings.explanation: The English carries a stray sentence-initial period into the displayed dialogue, visibly damaging the line.

findings.highlight: quite blunt.
findings.evidenceJa: 愛想というものはまったくない。
findings.governingReading: Kuzuki has absolutely no affability or social pleasantness.
findings.explanation: “Quite blunt” substitutes direct speech style for a total absence of warmth or charm.

findings.highlight: We will probably call the police.
findings.evidenceJa: おそらく刑事事件になるだろう。
findings.governingReading: Kuzuki expects the disappearance to become a criminal case.
findings.explanation: The English replaces the likely legal classification with the school’s act of calling police.

findings.highlight: do not spread the rumor.
findings.evidenceJa: 無闇に話す事は避けるように
findings.governingReading: Kuzuki instructs Issei to avoid discussing the matter indiscriminately.
findings.explanation: “Spread the rumor” narrows controlled disclosure of sensitive information into propagation of a rumor.

findings.highlight: Matou Shinji is absent today
findings.evidenceJa: 間桐慎二も無断欠席しており
findings.governingReading: Shinji too is absent without notice or permission.
findings.explanation: The English omits 無断, an important sign that his absence violates his normal rule-bound conduct.

findings.highlight: she does not know anything.
findings.evidenceJa: 事情は知らされていない
findings.governingReading: Sakura has not been informed of the circumstances.
findings.explanation: The English turns lack of being told the circumstances into total ignorance, removing the information-control relation.

findings.highlight: a student’s been missing since last night, and Shinji’s the last one to talk to that student
findings.evidenceJa: 昨日から行方不明の生徒がいて、その生徒と最後に会っていたのが慎二
findings.governingReading: A student has been missing since yesterday, and Shinji was the last person known to have met her.
findings.explanation: The English moves 昨日 to last night and narrows 会う, meeting or seeing her, to talking, altering the evidence summary.

findings.highlight: “Sorry to interrupt. I am sure the school’s curfew will be set at an earlier time now.”
findings.evidenceJa: そういった事情もある。
findings.governingReading: Kuzuki notes that those circumstances are also a reason for the school response.
findings.explanation: The English omits the connective sentence linking the disappearances to the expected earlier dismissal.

findings.highlight: the school’s curfew will be set at an earlier time now.
findings.evidenceJa: また下校時間が早まるだろう
findings.governingReading: The time students must leave school will probably be moved earlier again.
findings.explanation: “Curfew” introduces a different institutional rule and loses また, indicating a repeated early-dismissal measure.

findings.highlight: Quickly stating his business
findings.evidenceJa: 用件だけ述べて
findings.governingReading: Having stated only the necessary matter.
findings.explanation: The English changes exclusivity and Kuzuki’s laconic manner into speed.

findings.highlight: I should get some information out of him.
findings.evidenceJa: 無理にでも詳しい話を聞くべきだろう。
findings.governingReading: Despite the discourtesy, Shirou decides he should press Issei for the full details even if he must force the issue.
findings.explanation: The English removes both 詳しい and 無理にでも, weakening his urgency and deliberate intrusion.

findings.highlight: I already know Shinji hasn’t been home.
findings.evidenceJa: 慎二のヤツも捕まらないってのは判ったけど
findings.governingReading: Shirou understands that Shinji cannot be reached or found.
findings.explanation: The English substitutes not having been home, a different fact not stated in Shirou’s question.

findings.highlight: When we contacted the students who actually went to the club
findings.evidenceJa: 至急、練習に参加した生徒たちに話を聞いたところ
findings.governingReading: They urgently questioned the students who attended practice.
findings.explanation: The English omits 至急 and weakens direct fact-finding interviews into generic contact, while adding “actually.”

findings.highlight: When a student returned to school to get something he forgot
findings.evidenceJa: 忘れ物をした一年生が戻った時
findings.governingReading: When a first-year student returned for something forgotten.
findings.explanation: The English omits the student’s year and invents a male pronoun unsupported by the Japanese.

findings.highlight: the missing student and Shinji were having a quarrel.
findings.evidenceJa: 慎二とそいつが口喧嘩をしてたそうなんだ
findings.governingReading: Shinji and the missing student were reportedly having a verbal argument.
findings.explanation: Generic “quarrel” omits 口, leaving open a broader confrontation than the reported verbal dispute.

findings.highlight: There’s only one student that could’ve been there.
findings.evidenceJa: あの時、道場に残っている可能性があるとしたら、それは一人しかいない
findings.governingReading: If anyone could still have remained at the dojo at that time, there is only one possibility.
findings.explanation: The English drops remaining, the dojo anchor, and the explicit conditional inference, making the identification sound more direct.

findings.highlight: Don’t leave out the important detail
findings.evidenceJa: 肝心な話をぼかすな。
findings.governingReading: Do not blur or evade the essential point.
findings.explanation: “Leave out” frames the problem as omission, while ぼかす accuses Issei of withholding clarity or speaking evasively.

findings.highlight: after returning the archery range keys
findings.evidenceJa: 道場の鍵を職員室に戻した後
findings.governingReading: After Ayako returned the dojo key to the staff room.
findings.explanation: The English omits the staff-room destination, weakening the last-known-movements evidence.

findings.highlight: Issei averts his gaze.
findings.evidenceJa: 一成は言いづらそうに、視線を逸らしながらそう言った。
findings.governingReading: Issei says it as though the words are difficult to voice, averting his gaze.
findings.explanation: The English omits both his reluctant manner and the speech act, retaining only the gaze.

findings.highlight: all clubs are canceled for today.
findings.evidenceJa: 放課後の部活動は取りやめになっている。
findings.governingReading: After-school club activities have been called off.
findings.explanation: The English says the clubs themselves are canceled rather than their activities, producing an institutional category error.

findings.highlight: Her record of not being absent ends today
findings.evidenceJa: あいつの無遅刻無欠席もここで終わりだやね
findings.governingReading: Her record of neither tardiness nor absence ends here.
findings.explanation: The English omits 無遅刻, cutting the joke’s perfect-attendance formula in half.

findings.highlight: I wave goodbye and leave.
findings.evidenceJa: 片手をあげて教室を去る。
findings.governingReading: Shirou raises one hand and leaves the classroom.
findings.explanation: The English specifies a goodbye wave where the source gives only a raised-hand gesture.

findings.highlight: If there’s any place to go now, it’d be the archery range.
findings.evidenceJa: 他に何かあるとしたら、もう道場ぐらいしかない
findings.governingReading: If any other clue or possibility remains, only the dojo comes to mind.
findings.explanation: The English changes an evidentiary possibility into the practical question of where to go.

findings.highlight: Well, duh. There are no club activities today.
findings.evidenceJa: そうだよな、部活は休みなんだから
findings.governingReading: Of course no one is there, since club activities are canceled.
findings.explanation: “Well, duh” adds a conspicuously snide, contemporary voice absent from Shirou’s resigned self-correction.

findings.highlight: I guess I’ll talk to Issei. They might have some new information.
findings.evidenceJa: 一成に聞いてみるか。あれから何か判ったかもしれないし
findings.governingReading: Shirou will ask Issei, who may have learned something since lunch.
findings.explanation: The English changes the explicit singular referent Issei into unexplained plural “they.”

findings.highlight: it turned out nothing was wrong at all.
findings.evidenceJa: 聞いてみればなんでもない話だった
findings.governingReading: On asking, the whole matter might prove to be nothing serious.
findings.explanation: “Nothing was wrong at all” overstates the hoped-for outcome beyond なんでもない話, that the affair may be no great matter.

findings.highlight: We do not know where she went after returning the archery range keys, and after someone saw her in front of the archery range.
findings.evidenceJa: 彼女は道場の鍵を職員室に戻した後、弓道場前で見かけられてから一向に行方が知れない
findings.governingReading: After returning the dojo key to the staff room, Ayako was seen before the range and has been wholly unaccounted for ever since.
findings.explanation: The doubled “after … and after …” is grammatically broken and fails to present the ordered last-known-location sequence or 一向に’s emphatic continuing absence.

findings.highlight: I can’t go straight home
findings.evidenceJa: 何もせずに帰れる筈がない。
findings.governingReading: Shirou cannot possibly go home without doing anything after learning Ayako is missing.
findings.explanation: “Cannot go straight home” removes his moral refusal to leave the matter unattended and merely delays the trip home.

findings.highlight: She’s firm
findings.evidenceJa: あいつはしっかりしたヤツだし
findings.governingReading: Ayako is a reliable, level-headed person.
findings.explanation: Bare “firm” is unnatural and shifts しっかりした from reliability and sound judgment toward rigidity or physical firmness.

findings.highlight: Ayako-chan is absent today because she’s sick.
findings.evidenceJa: 綾子ちゃんなら風邪でお休みしてますよ？
findings.governingReading: The classmate says Ayako is absent with a cold.
findings.explanation: The English generalizes the specific cover story 風邪 into unspecified sickness.

findings.highlight: Even devils get sick, huh?
findings.evidenceJa: 鬼の霍乱サ。
findings.governingReading: The speaker jokes that even an extraordinarily robust person can be laid low by illness.
findings.explanation: Literal “devils get sick” obscures the fixed 鬼の霍乱 idiom and makes the line sound like a supernatural generalization.

findings.highlight: That’s all I could get from the girls in her class.
findings.evidenceJa: 帰り支度をしている女子の話は、決まってその程度でしかなかった。
findings.governingReading: The girls preparing to leave invariably offer accounts no deeper than that.
findings.explanation: The English makes the limitation Shirou’s failure to obtain more information rather than the consistent shallowness of the class story.

findings.highlight: It seems everyone has been told that Mitsuzuri is absent because of illness.
findings.evidenceJa: 二年Ａ組では、美綴はあくまで病欠という事になっている。
findings.governingReading: Within class 2-A, Ayako’s absence is being treated strictly as sick leave.
findings.explanation: The English invents an act of telling everyone and loses あくまで, the insistence that this remains the class’s official or surface account.

findings.highlight: I wipe my cheek with my uniform.
findings.evidenceJa: 制服の裾で頬を拭ってみる。
findings.governingReading: Shirou tries wiping his cheek with the hem of his uniform to test whether something is on his face.
findings.explanation: The English replaces the concrete hem with the whole uniform and drops みる, the exploratory attempt prompted by Rin’s stare.

findings.highlight: The classroom’s like always.
findings.evidenceJa: 別に、いつも通りの教室だよな
findings.governingReading: Shirou reassures himself that nothing in particular is wrong and the classroom is as usual.
findings.explanation: The English is conspicuously non-English and drops the self-confirming よな and dismissive 別に.

findings.highlight: the guys will take my food
findings.evidenceJa: 男どもにはハシをつつかれ
findings.governingReading: The boys reach their chopsticks into or pick at Shirou’s lunch.
findings.explanation: The English replaces the concrete intrusive chopstick action with taking his food, changing the teasing behavior.

findings.highlight: Wake me up when lunch is over.
findings.evidenceJa: 昼休みが終わる前に起こしてくれ
findings.governingReading: Issei asks to be awakened before lunch break ends.
findings.explanation: The English reverses 前に into “when … is over,” moving the wake-up to the deadline or after it.

findings.highlight: But sleep won’t let me rest, so I have to sleep to rest.
findings.evidenceJa: いくら眠っても疲れがとれない故、疲れをとる為に眠らざるを得ないのだ。
findings.governingReading: Because no amount of sleep removes Issei’s fatigue, he has no choice but to sleep in an attempt to relieve that fatigue.
findings.explanation: The English makes sleep the agent preventing rest and replaces the repeated fatigue mechanism with a different, nonsensical paradox.

findings.highlight: Man, it’s too early to be spring, you know?
findings.evidenceJa: はあ。春にはまだ早いんだけどな、一成
findings.governingReading: With a sigh, Shirou tells Issei it is still too early for spring, setting up the spring-sleep proverb.
findings.explanation: “Too early to be spring” is unidiomatic, “Man” replaces the sigh, and Issei’s name is omitted from the teasing address.

findings.highlight: Kuzuki-sensei stops his words
findings.evidenceJa: 葛木は言葉を止めた。
findings.governingReading: Kuzuki stops speaking when he notices Shirou.
findings.explanation: “Stops his words” copies Japanese structure into conspicuously unnatural English instead of expressing the interrupted speech.

findings.highlight: The student in the archery club said he saw her and Matou together.
findings.evidenceJa: あいつが昨日会っていたと、弓道部の一年が言っていたじゃないですか
findings.governingReading: The first-year reported that Shinji had met the missing student yesterday.
findings.explanation: The English makes the first-year explicitly see the pair together, strengthening an indirect report into direct eyewitness evidence and assigning unsupported male agency.
